name: IGO Group Sales CRM — Login Page
description: Design and UI spec for the live login screen, extracted directly from the current app source (src/pages/Login.jsx, src/components/RobotMascot.jsx, src/components/RobotScene.jsx, src/index.css). This documents what is actually implemented and running in the app today — it is a reference for a designer/developer, not a mockup.

typography.bodyFont: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif

tagline.text: Enter your details to access your workspace

screen.background: linear-gradient(180deg, #AEDCFB 0%, #D9EEFD 55%, #F4FAFF 100%) with three soft white radial highlights layered on top

shell.description: The white card holding both panes
shell.display: flex (two panes side by side on desktop)

panes.name: formPane
panes.contents: Logo, brand name, heading, tagline, Email/Phone segmented toggle, active form (email or phone), submit button

panes.contents: RobotScene (winter world + mascot), caption overlay pinned to bottom

hidden: 2nd and 3rd front trees (keeps exactly 1 per side)

prefersReducedMotion.description: All continuous animation loops are fully disabled

modeToggle.activeStyle: white pill background, shadow, dark text

fields.label: Email
fields.icon: EmailIcon (shown only when field is empty)

fields.icon: LockIcon (shown only when field is empty)

fields.label: Mobile number
fields.icon: CallsIcon (shown only when field is empty)

fields.label: Password
fields.icon: LockIcon (shown only when field is empty)

errorMessage.shownOnly: on sign-in failure, matches the actual auth error text

heroCaption.position: absolute, pinned to bottom of hero pane

mascotAndScene.concept: A layered-SVG robot character living inside a small animated winter/snow world, reacting live to what the user is doing on the form
mascotAndScene.architecture: RobotScene (environment: sky, clouds, mountains, trees, snow, particles, parallax) wraps RobotMascot (the character itself) as a child — fully separate components, the mascot never knows about the environment and vice versa

mascotStates.behavior: gentle breathing animation, idle antenna sway, one arm waves periodically, eyes track the cursor within a small range
neutral mouth swaps to a smile, eyes keep tracking cursor
both arms reposition to cover its eyes (privacy gesture), eyes narrow (scaleY 0.45), arm-wave animation stops
one-shot bounce animation, eyebrows raise, mouth switches to a happy expression
one-shot head-shake animation, eyebrows angle down/concerned, mouth switches to concerned expression, auto-reverts to idle after 2.2s

mascotAndScene.eyeAndHeadTracking: Head and eyes independently ease toward the real mouse cursor position every animation frame via direct CSS custom-property writes (no React re-render per frame) — decoupled from the environment's own parallax system

environmentLayers.detail: soft blue gradient background on the hero pane itself
layered, each with its own slow horizontal drift animation (36–52s loops) plus a small mouse-parallax multiplier (3–6px), fluffy white/pale-blue gradient fill
two-tone pale blue jagged SVG silhouette, barely moves on parallax (2px multiplier)
hand-drawn layered SVG pine trees in a back row (smaller, faded, more parallax) and a front row (larger, full opacity, most parallax) — 4 trees per row on desktop
rounded white-to-pale-blue gradient mound along the bottom of the scene, plus two smaller snow-bank bumps
small falling dots with staggered durations (9–15s) and delays, fade in/out, fixed 420px fall distance

parallax.trigger: real mouse movement anywhere on the page
parallax.mechanism: target position eases toward the cursor at a 0.08 ease factor per animation frame, written to --parallax-x/--parallax-y CSS custom properties
parallax.note: Independent of the mascot's own head/eye cursor-tracking system

behaviorNotes: No message is sent or account created automatically anywhere on this screen — it only authenticates against the existing Supabase Auth backend.
Switching between Email/Phone mode resets any error and returns the mascot to idle.
This JSON describes the screen exactly as implemented and currently live in the app — the app itself is unchanged by exporting this file.
